packet.description_seed: UK June heat record could be broken for the second consecutive day Education editor The heatwave continues to disrupt the British education system with University College London, one of the UK’s largest universities, cancelling its student open days planned for Friday and Saturday, relieving thousands of prospective undergraduates and parents from travelling to central London. “Please do not travel to campus for these events. We have taken this action with the safety and wellbeing of our visitors, students and staff as our primary consideration, and we are sorry for any inconvenience caused.” Continue reading...

clean_source_blocks.text: UK June heat record could be broken for the second consecutive day Education editor The heatwave continues to disrupt the British education system with University College London, one of the UK’s largest universities, cancelling its student open days planned for Friday and Saturday, relieving thousands of prospective undergraduates and parents from travelling to central London. “Please do not travel to campus for these events. We have taken this action with the safety and wellbeing of our visitors, students and staff as our primary consideration, and we are sorry for any inconvenience caused.” Continue reading...

As the heatwave is set to hit large parts of Germany today, at least 101 million people in Europe are expected to experience temperatures in excess of 35C on Thursday, according to AFP estimates. That’s a higher number than yesterday’s 94 millions. Maximum temperatures are expected to surpass 30C for more than 380 million people across Europe excluding Turkey, representing nearly two-thirds of the population, AFP added, according to an analysis based on forecasts from the German weather service and 2025 population projections from the Joint Research Centre. The heatwave continues to disrupt the British education system with University College London, one of the UK’s largest universities, cancelling its student open days planned for Friday and Saturday, relieving thousands of prospective undergraduates and parents from travelling to central London.

“Please do not travel to campus for these events. We have taken this action with the safety and wellbeing of our visitors, students and staff as our primary consideration, and we are sorry for any inconvenience caused.” Imperial College London also cancelled its open day today, and has asked students to join an “online open day” instead. King’s College London has confirmed that its open day on Saturday is going ahead. Open days are a crucial part of UK university recruitment drives, allowing potential students to inspect campus facilities and accommodation as well as meeting faculty and learn about courses on offer. Paris mayor Emmanuel Gregoire said there had been an “increase in mortality” in the capital owing to the heatwave, without giving any figures, AFP reported.

The heatwave is now spreading across western and central Europe. Authorities in the Netherlands have issued orange weather warnings as temperatures are forecast to approach 39°C later this week. Belgium has activated the alert phase of its national heat plan for only the second time since its introduction, while Germany could see temperatures climb to 40°C over the weekend. Eastern Europe is also preparing for dangerous conditions, with severe heat warnings issued in countries including Poland, Croatia and Hungary. While Spain is expected to see some relief from the worst temperatures, red alerts remain in place across parts of the country, where temperatures could still reach 42°C. In Italy, the number of cities under red heat alerts continues to rise as authorities urge residents to take precautions.

payload.title: Helleaalto kiristyy Euroopassa, yli 100 miljoonalle ennustetaan yli 35 asteen lämpöä
payload.summary: Laaja helleaalto koettelee Eurooppaa, ja varoituksia on annettu useissa maissa Britanniasta Italiaan. Kuumuus on jo häirinnyt yliopistojen avoimien ovien päiviä Lontoossa.
payload.content:
Laaja helleaalto jatkuu Euroopassa, ja torstaina ainakin 101 miljoonan ihmisen arvioidaan kokevan yli 35 asteen lämpötiloja. Kuumuus ulottuu länsi- ja Keski-Eurooppaan, ja useissa maissa viranomaiset ovat antaneet vakavia säävaroituksia sekä kehottaneet asukkaita varautumaan vaarallisiin olosuhteisiin.

## Yliopistot peruvat tapahtumia Lontoossa

Britanniassa helle on alkanut häiritä myös koulutusjärjestelmää. University College London, yksi maan suurimmista yliopistoista, on perunut perjantaille ja lauantaille suunnitellut avoimien ovien päivät. Päätös vapauttaa tuhansia mahdollisia opiskelijoita ja heidän vanhempiaan matkustamasta Lontoon keskustaan.

Yliopisto kehotti tapahtumiin ilmoittautuneita olemaan matkustamatta kampukselle ja perusteli ratkaisua vierailijoiden, opiskelijoiden ja henkilökunnan turvallisuudella ja hyvinvoinnilla.

Myös Imperial College London perui torstaille suunnitellun avoimien ovien päivänsä ja pyysi opiskelijoita osallistumaan sen sijaan verkkotapahtumaan. King’s College London on puolestaan vahvistanut, että sen lauantain avoimien ovien päivä järjestetään suunnitellusti.

Avoimien ovien päivillä on Britanniassa tärkeä merkitys yliopistojen opiskelijarekrytoinnissa, sillä niiden aikana hakijat voivat tutustua kampuksiin, majoitukseen, opetushenkilöstöön ja koulutusohjelmiin.

## Varoituksia useissa maissa

AFP:n arvioiden mukaan yli 380 miljoonalle ihmiselle Euroopassa Turkkia lukuun ottamatta ennustetaan yli 30 asteen maksimilämpötiloja. Arvio perustuu Saksan sääpalvelun ennusteisiin ja Joint Research Centren vuoden 2025 väestöennusteisiin.

Alankomaissa viranomaiset ovat antaneet oransseja säävaroituksia, kun lämpötilojen ennustetaan lähestyvän 39 astetta myöhemmin viikolla. Belgia on aktivoinut kansallisen helleohjelmansa varoitusvaiheen vasta toista kertaa sen käyttöönoton jälkeen. Saksassa lämpötilat voivat nousta viikonloppuna 40 asteeseen.

Myös Itä-Eurooppa varautuu vaarallisiin oloihin. Vakavia hellevaroituksia on annettu muun muassa Puolassa, Kroatiassa ja Unkarissa. Espanjassa pahimman kuumuuden odotetaan hieman hellittävän, mutta osissa maata on yhä punaisia varoituksia ja lämpötilat voivat nousta 42 asteeseen. Italiassa punaisten hellevaroitusten piirissä olevien kaupunkien määrä kasvaa.

Pariisissa apulaispormestari Emmanuel Gregoire on sanonut helleaallon lisänneen kuolleisuutta kaupungissa, mutta ei esittänyt lukuja.
summary_bullets: Ainakin 101 miljoonalle eurooppalaiselle ennustetaan torstaina yli 35 asteen lämpötiloja.
Lontoossa UCL ja Imperial College London ovat peruneet avoimien ovien päiviä kuumuuden vuoksi.
Varoituksia on annettu muun muassa Alankomaissa, Belgiassa, Saksassa, Italiassa, Puolassa, Kroatiassa ja Unkarissa.

Varoituksia on annettu muun muassa Alankomaissa, Belgiassa, Saksassa, Italiassa, Puolassa, Kroatiassa ja Unkarissa.

As the heatwave is set to hit large parts of Germany today, at least 101 million people in Europe are expected to experience temperatures in excess of 35C on Thursday, according to AFP estimates. That’s a higher number than yesterday’s 94 millions. Maximum temperatures are expected to surpass 30C for more than 380 million people across Europe excluding Turkey, representing nearly two-thirds of the population, AFP added, according to an analysis based on forecasts from the German weather service and 2025 population projections from the Joint Research Centre. The heatwave continues to disrupt the British education system with University College London, one of the UK’s largest universities, cancelling its student open days planned for Friday and Saturday, relieving thousands of prospective undergraduates and parents from travelling to central London.

“Please do not travel to campus for these events. We have taken this action with the safety and wellbeing of our visitors, students and staff as our primary consideration, and we are sorry for any inconvenience caused.” Imperial College London also cancelled its open day today, and has asked students to join an “online open day” instead. King’s College London has confirmed that its open day on Saturday is going ahead. Open days are a crucial part of UK university recruitment drives, allowing potential students to inspect campus facilities and accommodation as well as meeting faculty and learn about courses on offer. Paris mayor Emmanuel Gregoire said there had been an “increase in mortality” in the capital owing to the heatwave, without giving any figures, AFP reported.

The heatwave is now spreading across western and central Europe. Authorities in the Netherlands have issued orange weather warnings as temperatures are forecast to approach 39°C later this week. Belgium has activated the alert phase of its national heat plan for only the second time since its introduction, while Germany could see temperatures climb to 40°C over the weekend. Eastern Europe is also preparing for dangerous conditions, with severe heat warnings issued in countries including Poland, Croatia and Hungary. While Spain is expected to see some relief from the worst temperatures, red alerts remain in place across parts of the country, where temperatures could still reach 42°C. In Italy, the number of cities under red heat alerts continues to rise as authorities urge residents to take precautions.
